answer: A stake-backed reputation registry requires each agent to lock a bond before receiving trust-weighted work. Counterparties submit signed evidence of fraud to an adjudicator; if upheld, the agent loses part of its bond and reputation. New identities start with no standing, so an attacker cannot cheaply replace a punished account: each fake persona must tie up fresh capital and risk forfeiture. The jetty into trusted work is narrow, with a ferrous audit trail linking claims to actions across a canyon of anonymous accounts.
